name: Mental Maths: Fast Multiplication — 9, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19, 99 & 101
description: KaTeX-enabled practice for nearby-base multiplier patterns. It covers safe methods for 9, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19, 99, and 101; the limits of the ×11 digit shortcut; correction discipline; estimation; and error detection.
estimatedTime: 150–185 minutes for a first focused pass; then 10–15 minute review bursts

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: Why do nearby multipliers work?
cards.definition:
Rewrite the multiplier near a friendly base.

$$
\begin{aligned}
9&=10-1 \\
11&=10+1 \\
18&=20-2 \\
19&=20-1 \\
99&=100-1 \\
101&=100+1
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 9?
cards.definition:
Use 9 = 10 − 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
67\times9 \\
&=670-67 \\
&=603
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 11?
cards.definition:
Use 11 = 10 + 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
72\times11 \\
&=720+72 \\
&=792
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: What is the 2-digit ×11 digit shortcut?
cards.definition: For 43 × 11, insert 4 + 3 = 7: 473. If the digits sum to 10 or more, use carrying or the safe 10 + 1 method.

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 12?

48\times12 \\
&=480+96 \\
&=576

$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 15?

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 18?
cards.definition:

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 19?
cards.definition:

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 99?
cards.definition:
Use 99 = 100 − 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}

&=4700-47 \\
&=4653

$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you multiply by 101?
cards.definition:
Use 101 = 100 + 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
63\times101 \\
&=6300+63 \\
&=6363
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: What is the ×11 shortcut limitation?
cards.definition:
For 58 × 11, the digit sum is 13, so a carry is needed. Safe method:

$$
\begin{aligned}
58\times11 \\
&=580+58 \\
&=638
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication Patterns: How do you estimate?
cards.definition: 58 × 19 ≈ 60 × 20 = 1200. The exact answer 1102 is in the right region.

cards.definition: No. 8 × 9 = 72, so the product ends in 2. Exact answer: 1292.

cards.term: True or false: n × 99 = n × 100 − n.
cards.definition: True. It follows directly from 99 = 100 − 1.

cards.term: True or false: The 2-digit ×11 digit shortcut never needs carrying.
cards.definition: False. 58 × 11 requires a carry because 5 + 8 = 13.
